key_insight: A 145,281-parameter multi-head quantum module replaced eight contiguous transformer blocks in a 30-billion-parameter LLM, displacing 16.33% of its parameters.
engineering_relevance: Partitioning hidden states into small quantum heads enables NISQ-compatible integration into production-scale LLM architectures without encoding the entire hidden space at once.
method: Partition 2,048 hidden dimensions into 32 heads, each angle-encoded on 8 qubits.
Process heads with depth-L=4 quantum circuits and learned readouts, coupled through constrained classical mixers.
Train using exact statevector simulation, then execute fusion-checkpoint quantum heads on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor.
evidence_signal: Held-out perplexity ablations found mixer-only fused modules within 1–3% of the full module, while a parameter-matched classical MLP remained a few percent better.
watch_item: Quantum advantage is not established: limited-seed non-entangling and frozen-circuit controls outperformed the full module, and training used classical simulation.
paper_title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
